APOLLOTYRE: Andhra Pradesh Capacity Buildout Will Support Future Earnings Power Visibility
news.body: The analyst fair value estimate for Apollo Tyres has been revised from about ₹534 to about ₹476, as analysts adjust their P/E assumptions and margins while still factoring in ongoing revenue growth expectations supported by recent sector research on alternative asset managers. Analyst Commentary Analysts are using recent research on global alternative asset managers as a reference point when thinking about Apollo Tyres, especially around what multiples to apply and how much earnings power to ascribe to future cycles.

news.title: Consensus EPS estimates fall by 20%, revenue upgraded
news.body: The consensus outlook for fiscal year 2027 has been updated. 2027 revenue forecast increased from ₹309.5b to ₹317.9b. EPS estimate fell from ₹32.21 to ₹25.66 per share. Net income forecast to grow 18% next year vs 23% growth forecast for Auto Components industry in India. Consensus price target down from ₹534 to ₹476. Share price fell 7.4% to ₹372 over the past week.

news.title: Price target decreased by 9.9% to ₹481
news.body: Down from ₹534, the current price target is an average from 23 analysts. New target price is 28% above last closing price of ₹375. Stock is down 23% over the past year. The company is forecast to post earnings per share of ₹25.99 for next year compared to ₹21.66 last year.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS misses analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹21.66 (up from ₹17.66 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹286.0b (up 9.5% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹13.7b (up 22% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 4.8% (up from 4.3% in FY 2025). Revenue was in line with analyst estimates. Earnings per share (EPS) missed analyst estimates by 14%. Revenue is forecast to grow 7.1% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 11% growth forecast for the Auto Components industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 13% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 2% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Andhra Pradesh Capacity Buildout Will Support Long Term Earnings Power
news.body: Analysts have kept the fair value estimate for Apollo Tyres steady at ₹534.17, with only marginal adjustments to the discount rate, revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E assumptions guiding this latest price target update. Analyst Commentary Recent Street research around Apollo linked entities has focused on shifts in price targets and reassessments of earnings assumptions, which offer a useful backdrop when you think about Apollo Tyres’ own valuation and execution risks.

This reflects analysts factoring in a modestly higher discount rate, steady revenue growth expectations around 7%, and a small trim to projected profit margins and future P/E assumptions.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Upside Hinges On Andhra Pradesh Capacity Expansion Delivery
news.body: Analysts have trimmed the Apollo Tyres price target from about ₹558.61 to roughly ₹539.74. This reflects slightly higher discounting, a marginally different revenue growth and profit margin profile, and a modestly lower assumed future P/E multiple.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Returns Will Reflect Andhra Pradesh Expansion And Cash Deployment Discipline
news.body: Analysts have kept our fair value estimate for Apollo Tyres steady at ₹562.71 per share, with only marginal tweaks to the discount rate and long term assumptions. This reflects broadly unchanged views on revenue growth, profit margins and future P/E despite recent recalibration of price targets across the wider alternatives and credit space.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Returns Will Reflect Capacity Expansion And Refined Earnings Assumptions
news.body: The latest analyst update on Apollo Tyres reflects a modest recalibration of assumptions, with the long term fair value held around ₹562.71 per share while analysts factor in slightly higher discount rates and revenue growth expectations, along with a small adjustment to profit margin and future P/E inputs. Analyst Commentary Recent Street research around Apollo branded entities has focused on recalibrating price targets rather than making sweeping calls.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Returns Will Reflect Refined Earnings Assumptions And Governance Watchpoints

Analyst Commentary Recent Street research around the broader Apollo group has focused on adjustments to price targets and views on future execution, which can offer some read across on how analysts think about valuation, growth and risk for names like Apollo Tyres as well.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues exceed analyst expectations
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹7.43 (up from ₹5.31 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹77.9b (up 13% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹4.71b (up 40% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 6.0% (up from 4.9% in 3Q 2025). Revenue exceeded analyst estimates by 2.9%. Earnings per share (EPS) also surpassed analyst estimates by 8.4%. Revenue is forecast to grow 6.4% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 10% growth forecast for the Auto Components industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 9% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 15% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Returns Will Reflect Refined Earnings Assumptions And Supportive Capital Markets
news.body: Analysts have nudged their fair value estimate for Apollo Tyres slightly higher to ₹569.33 from ₹562.83, citing small refinements in projected revenue growth, profit margins and future P/E assumptions, while keeping discount rate expectations broadly unchanged. Analyst Commentary Recent Street research on related Apollo entities has focused on how valuation targets are being fine tuned rather than completely reset.

news.title: APOLLOTYRE: Future Returns Will Balance Credit Risks With Fee And Capital Markets Tailwinds
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their price target on Apollo Tyres slightly, cutting it by INR 3 to reflect a more cautious stance on near term credit conditions, even as they acknowledge ongoing tailwinds from capital markets activity and fee driven earnings. Analyst Commentary Analysts remain divided on Apollo Tyres, with recent target cuts framed more as valuation housekeeping than a thesis change, as they balance solid fee based growth drivers against a more uncertain credit backdrop.
